content: Look outside your window! What are those green things standing still but growing taller every day? Some are taller than your house, and some are smaller than your shoe! Have you ever wondered what they are? They are the green magic of nature!
Imagine you couldn't walk, run, or play games, but you could make your own food just by standing in the bright sunlight! What do you think you would be?

content.title: Seed to Plant
content.description: Watch how a tiny seed wakes up in the soil and stretches its leaves towards the sun!

content: Yes! They are called Plants (Paudhe)! They are living things just like us, but they stay in one place. They drink water from the soil and eat sunlight.

definition: A living thing that grows in the earth and has a stem, leaves, and roots.

question: Are plants living things?
options: Yes, they grow and need water

content: Go touch a small leaf gently. How does it feel? Think about how a plant drinks water without a mouth! They drink from their roots hidden in the ground, just like drinking from a straw.
Remind students that just like they need food and water to grow, plants need sunlight and water! This connects to our previous chapter on 'Living Things'.
Draw a plant you see near your house. Make sure to color its leaves green!
Have you ever tried to hug a huge Mango tree? It's too big! But you can easily hold a tiny Tulsi plant in one hand. Why are they so different?
If you were a little bird, would you build your nest on a tiny grass plant or a giant tree? Why do you think birds choose tall places?

content.title: Trees vs Small Plants
content.description: See the thick, strong trunk of the tree compared to the thin, soft stem of the small plant.

content: Very big, tall, and strong plants are called Trees (Ped). They have thick, hard stems called a trunk. Small plants have soft, green stems!

definition: A very tall and big plant with a strong, wooden trunk.

content: Students often think all green things are trees. Remember, only the very tall and strong ones with woody trunks are trees! A small rose plant is not a tree.

question: Which of these is a Tree?

content: Look at your own arms. Some people have thick arms, some have thin arms. Trees have thick, hard trunks to stand strong in the wind!
In ancient India, big trees like the Banyan tree (Vat Vriksha) and Peepal tree were respected as sacred givers of life. They provide cool shade to entire villages and homes for thousands of birds.
Next time you go to a park, find the biggest tree. Try to give it a big hug and see if your hands can touch on the other side!
